messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just got word from a reliable source — things are shifting quietly. The usual cracks are showing in the system, and people are starting to act like they expect something to happen, not just talk about it. Keep your heads down, watch the rhythms, and stay sharp — the air feels different than it has in years."
Sender 2: "Just wanted to say — things feel different lately. The usual quiet has shifted; even the most careful people are talking in half-words now. Noticed a few familiar faces pulling back from routine routines, and the markets seem too busy for just normal life. Keep your ears open, but your mouth shut. We’re not rushing anything — just staying sharp."
Sender 3: "The markets are quiet, but the air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under something big. I’ve been told the hospital’s stockpiling meds again, and the broadcast blackout yesterday wasn’t a glitch. If we’re all feeling this, they must be too."
Sender 4: "The pharmacy’s been quiet lately—my neighbor’s been stocking up on meds, and the new cadets graduated with full fanfare. Things feel… paused, like everyone’s holding their breath. Just keep your head down, and make sure your supply of painkillers isn’t running low."
Sender 5: "The air feels different — like something’s shifting under the surface. Just heard the clinic’s been stockpiling meds quietly, and the usual silence around budget reports is starting to speak louder than words. Stay sharp, keep lines open, and don’t trust the silence."
Sender 6: "Things are shifting quietly — noticed more people reconnecting, even at work, and the usual rigidity’s letting up. Just keep your head down, stay sharp, and trust your instincts more than the news."
Sender 7: "Just heard from someone in the city — the power cuts are getting worse, and people are talking more openly than they have in years. I’ve been keeping my phone off the charger lately, just in case. Let’s keep it light when we meet."
Sender 8: "The city feels different lately — not tense, exactly, but… expectant. Like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see if the cracks we’re noticing are just fading or if something’s about to shift. Be careful what you say, and keep your plans light — just in case."
Sender 9: "Just got back from the market—same as always, but everyone’s moving slower, like they’re holding their breath. I’ve been hearing the same quiet questions from people I don’t even know. Something’s shifting, and I think we’re past the point of waiting. Keep your head down, but your eyes open."
Sender 10: "Just got word from someone close to the inner circle — things are shifting beneath the surface. The usual rhythms are holding, but there’s a quiet unease in the air, and people are already making plans beyond next month. Keep your eyes open, but don’t say anything."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
